units.translation: In the manuscripts of the tragedians sometimes wrongly written πράττειν [to do], as at Ag. 1331.
about Helen, the author of many evils

Thus I corrected for δικαίως [justly], which is in M, but ou in an erasure, with w written above by an old hand, which is δικαίως [justly]. The corrector did not notice that from the adjective δίκαιος [just] δικαίως [justly] must be understood with the verb πρᾶξαι [to do].

thus Schuetz for ἅπερ [which things]. where the scholiast says: κατεσκεύασε δὲ τὸ τὸ μασχαλισθῆναι αὐτὸν ἡ Κλυταιμνήστρα [Clytemnestra contrived his mutilation]. ἢ καὶ οὕτως ἀτίμως αὐτὸν θάψασα δυστυχίαν μεγίστην κατασκευάζουσα τῷ σῷ βίῳ, ὦ Ὀρέστα [or, having buried him so dishonorably, she is preparing the greatest misfortune for your life, Orestes] · ὅ ἐστιν, ἵνα δυστυχή βίον Ζήσης, τοῦ Ἀγαμέμνονος μὴ δυναμένου σοι συμμαχῆσαι πρὸς τὴν τιμωρίαν Κλυταιμνήστρας [that is, so that you may live a miserable life, since Agamemnon is unable to help you in avenging Clytemnestra].
where Stanley conjectured ἐπαχθῆ [burdensome].
where κότον [anger] is suspect, on which see the note.

χἀρπαγὰς [and plunderings] Tyrwhitt. ὑπερκόπους [excessive] Heath. which he explained by ἀπητήσαμεν, ἤτοι καθείλομεν [we demanded, that is, we destroyed], Triclinius changed to ἐφραξάμεσθα [we fenced ourselves], which should rather be written ἐφαρξάμεσθα [we fenced ourselves].
thus Porson for πράττειν [to do]
without judgment I did everything
What must I do or say to do things dear to the gods?
the bridle of Zeus forced him to do these things by violence
the one who did these things
he did as he accomplished
enacting the signs of tyranny against the city
and so I did
he brought about an unendurable grief
as we did
do it, fatten yourself, polluting justice
but if I must do something else more prudent
I approve of doing these things as one accountable
do what has been commanded
if you do these things
having fared well
you did everything
for I know that you are pondering some things deeply, but openly doing others more calmly
you wish to hear rather than to act justly
having done these things
having performed cutting and releasing remedies for these things
you would do as one who has met the Argive army
I would not do these things without the people
you both gladden my heart by speaking and by doing
having rendered aid
let us not bring shame upon ourselves, but pleasure to my enemies
what fair voyage did they accomplish?
I do these things eagerly for these citizens
for those who now transgress my oaths, we will bring about helpless misfortunes – so that toil may be repentance for them
will you do this so that I have such strength?
he was mutilated, so that you may know this. | And she did as she buries him, | seeking to establish a fate | unbearable for your life
you hear what has been done
the things done to the dead
the deed is done
for it has been done well
upon these things that have been done
the things now done
of the things done long ago
what deed have you done except to cause evils?
all things have been done except to rule over the gods
thinking that my son will exact retribution for these things
Justice, exacting what is owed, cries out greatly
the one who committed the murder of his father
Justice exacts the anger of the dead man
the gods – those who were jointly responsible for my return and for the just things I did to the city of Priam
the dishonoring of the tables in later time and of Zeus of the hearth, exacting the bridal honor, openly honoring
and we exacted excessive penalties
